Somers' D (Somers' Delta)

Source: R/somersDelta.R
somersDelta.Rd

Computes Somers' D, an asymmetric measure of association for ordinal variables. The function provides interfaces for both contingency tables and paired vectors.

somersDelta(x, y = NULL, conf.level = NA, direction = c("row", "column"))

Arguments

x

a numeric vector or a contingency table (matrix or table)

y

optional numeric vector. If supplied, must have the same length as x.

conf.level

confidence level for confidence intervals. If NA, no confidence interval is returned.

direction

direction for contingency tables: "row" (default) computes \(D(Y|X)\), while "column" computes \(D(X|Y)\)

Value

if conf.level = NA, a numeric scalar. Otherwise a named numeric vector with elements:

est

point estimate of Somers' D

lci

lower confidence interval bound

uci

upper confidence interval bound

Details

Somers' D is a directional measure of association related to Kendall's \(\tau_b\) and Goodman–Kruskal's Gamma. It differs from Gamma in that it corrects only for ties on the dependent variable.

For two variables \(X\) and \(Y\), Somers' D is defined as

$$D(Y|X) = \frac{C - D}{C + D + T_Y}$$

where \(C\) and \(D\) denote the number of concordant and discordant pairs, and \(T_Y\) the number of pairs tied on the dependent variable.

Somers' D takes values in \([-1, 1]\). Values close to \(1\) indicate strong positive association, values close to \(-1\) strong negative association.

Direction:

  • For vectors: somersDelta(x, y) estimates \(D(Y|X)\).

  • Reversing the order, somersDelta(y, x), estimates \(D(X|Y)\).

  • For tables: direction="row" computes \(D(Y|X)\), direction="column" computes \(D(X|Y)\).

Somers' D is appropriate only when both variables are ordinal.

References

Agresti, A. (2002) Categorical Data Analysis. John Wiley & Sons, pp. 57–59.

Brown, M. B., & Benedetti, J. K. (1977). Sampling behavior of tests for correlation in two-way contingency tables. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 72, 309–315.

Goodman, L. A., & Kruskal, W. H. (1954). Measures of association for cross classifications. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 49, 732–764.

Somers, R. H. (1962). A new asymmetric measure of association for ordinal variables. American Sociological Review, 27, 799–811.

Goodman, L. A., & Kruskal, W. H. (1963). Measures of association for cross classifications III. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 58, 310–364.

See also

somers2 (restricted to binary response),

Other assoc.ordinal: cStat(), conDisPairs(), gkGamma(), gkTau(), kendallTauA(), kendallTauB(), kendallW(), stuartTauC()

Examples


# Example from SAS documentation (PROC FREQ)
# https://support.sas.com/documentation/
#
# Reported values:
# Somers' D C|R = 0.4427 (95% CI: 0.2786, 0.6068)
# Somers' D R|C = 0.2569 (95% CI: 0.1592, 0.3547)

tab <- as.table(rbind(
  c(26,26,23,18,9),
  c(6,7,9,14,23)
))

# D(Y|X)  (row direction)
somersDelta(tab, direction="row", conf.level=0.95)
#>       est       lci       uci 
#> 0.2569444 0.1592938 0.3545951 

# D(X|Y)  (column direction)
somersDelta(tab, direction="column", conf.level=0.95)
#>       est       lci       uci 
#> 0.4426720 0.2785571 0.6067869 

# Vector interface
somersDelta(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
#> [1] -0.7300613
